Q: How to upgrade all Python packages with pip A:

Having issues with syntax and freeze options not supported in Termux, this one liner works for me. I had to do a regular listing because it offers the option of only listing outdated.

pip list -o|xargs -I {} sh -c 'pkg="{}";pkg="${pkg%% *}";case "$pkg" in (Package|------------------|pip) ;; (*) pip install -U "$pkg";; esac;'

For testing, you can use "-u" (list only updated) instead of "-o" (list only outdated). I use simple regular expression %% to truncate after first space. Then I use a clean case statement which uses syntax which runs well inside an xargs subshell. The case statement looks for the first two garbage lines (or pip which is no longer upgraded via pip), and does nothing, and then does a pip install -U on everything else.

Q: Spring Microservice or Spring Modulith .... When? A:

The "best idea" depends on what you define as "best" (aka. the metric for "best"). It is certainly a valid idea. If the modulith is properly modularized, then extracting a module in a microservice (when necessary/desired) shouldn't be too hard (granted, the Interface between the services has to be designed).

Q: Performance of deleting multiple rows in batch A:

It sounds like the EAV model and one of its many drawbacks.

The table and indices should vacuum themselves automatically and you can tune that behaviour a bit. You could also adjust their fillfactor to encourage in-page space re-use independent of the vacuuming schedule.

You could also revisit the topic of (de-)normalisation. Storing each form as a jsonb is still clunky, but it might turn out lighter, faster and easier to work with than EAV - here's an example comparison.

Q: pip install oracledb takes ~9 minutes on Alpine (musl) because no musllinux wheel, how to avoid building from source in Docker? A:

This is a well-known problem: https://pythonspeed.com/articles/alpine-docker-python/ . For your case it's recommended to avoid Alpine and switch to Debian/Ubuntu/RedHat.

For Alpine the way to speed up is to build from sources once and use shared cache. Read https://pythonspeed.com/articles/speeding-up-docker-ci/ and https://pythonspeed.com/articles/faster-pip-installs/

Q: What is the “|=” (vertical bar, equals sign) assignment operator in Python? A:

It's just an operator of logical OR. If total_mask is

0011101010101001110

and is_NA is

0000000000000100000

then total_mask will become

0011101010101101110

in this case it's just like addition.

Of course the numbers are here written in binary. In Python you can convert a number to a binary string using the bin function, for example

>>> bin(99)
'0b1100011'

Q: What is the best approach to writing a personal config symlink management scriptfor linux? A:
  • set -euo pipefail → Dangerous pointless cargo-cult that most LLM models carries.
  • ALL_UPPERCASE variable → Cargo cult from 1970's where computers only supported upper-case letters. Counter-productive, and augment the risk of environment-variables collisions.

Maybe you could continue to ask an LLM about your question while making it clear you don't want cargo-cult counter-productive shell bad practice.

Current LLM are not trained with quality material in Shell. LLMs were trained on a lot of decades-old obsolete shell scripts or amateurish throw-away content.

Good guidance for shell exist, but you will have to read it and construct your experience. And sometimes the shell is not a good tool for all problems.

A lot of good Shell knowledge to read and explore: https://mywiki.wooledge.org/FullBashFAQ
